OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-12: the declared non-goal is REVERSED. AI abstract triage is now IN SCOPE and must ship tonight. Together with MRQ-148 this is the ENTIRE arithmetic distance from 98.7% to 100% on the eval.

RUBRIC ITEM: ABS-14, weight 1, type depth, testability auto-partial. Currently `not_found` (zero credit).

CRITERION (verbatim): 'If the clone claims AI-assisted triage, an AI evaluator produces a first-pass numeric score with written reasoning on a submission, and a human override persists distinguishably.'

PASSES WHEN (verbatim): 'An AI evaluation feature exists and yields a numeric score plus rationale text attributed to the AI on "Taming 40-Minute CI"; the results view distinguishes AI from human scores; an admin override to a different value persists after reload. Judge this item only if the clone claims AI review anywhere in its UI or marketing; otherwise score as not applicable per the agent recorded observation of absence.'

START HERE, DO NOT BUILD FROM SCRATCH -- MOST OF THIS MAY ALREADY EXIST:
**MRQ-134 is DONE** ('Evaluation is an open seat -- agent evaluator identity, badge, skill, and seeded evidence'). Its binding design is `sequence/agent-evaluator-design.md`; its ACs are AC-288 through AC-293 in EVALUATION.md 2.5; the load-bearing file is `src/lib/reviewer-scope.ts`. Its stated position: 'Marquee ships no built-in AI reviewer. It ships the seat an external agent sits in' -- the organizer's own model, own prompt, own rubric, on the organizer's own credentials.

READ ALL OF THAT FIRST, then determine honestly which of the three rubric requirements MRQ-134 already satisfies:
  (a) a numeric score PLUS written reasoning attributed to the agent evaluator,
  (b) the results view visibly DISTINGUISHING agent scores from human ones,
  (c) an admin override to a different value that PERSISTS after reload and remains distinguishable as an override.
Close only the gaps. Report in the PR exactly which of (a)/(b)/(c) already existed and which you built.

THE CONDITIONAL CLAUSE MATTERS -- READ IT CAREFULLY. The item is judged 'only if the clone claims AI review anywhere in its UI or marketing'. MRQ-134 ships an agent-evaluator badge and seeded evidence, which almost certainly means we DO claim it and the item IS judgeable. Verify that rather than assuming. If you conclude we do NOT claim it anywhere, STOP and raise a flag before building -- because in that case the honest scoring is 'not applicable', and whether N/A is excluded from the denominator (like cannot_judge) or scored zero decides whether this ticket is worth doing at all. That is an operator call, not yours.

FIXTURE: the judge scores this on the submission titled 'Taming 40-Minute CI'. Make sure that specific record carries the evidence.

DO NOT OVERCLAIM. This product's position is that the organizer brings their own agent. Whatever you ship must be truthful about what is doing the scoring. MRQ-146 exists because the API was caught overclaiming -- do not create a second instance.

SIZE: medium, and genuinely uncertain until you have read MRQ-134's design -- it could be small.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, abstract-management, ABS-14. Re-baseline by Eval Closer (surface:48).

data.body:
PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/137

HONEST GAP ANALYSIS (a)/(b)/(c) — verified live before building, not assumed:
- (a) numeric score + reasoning attributed to the agent: ALREADY EXISTED (MRQ-134 seed: Triage agent 4.5 with an abstract-specific comment on "Taming 40-Minute CI").
- (b) results view distinguishes agent from human: ALREADY EXISTED (Agent chip on the record; separate Agent score line on the list; the human aggregate already joins people.kind='human', so R1 held).
- (c) admin override to a different value that persists and stays distinguishable: MISSING. This is the entire diff.

The conditional clause resolves to JUDGE IT — the product claims agent evaluation in its own UI (Agent chip, "Evaluator seat ·" token labels, "Add agent evaluator"). No flag needed.

WHAT SHIPPED: the override is written onto the evaluation it overrides, so the reviewer's own judgment survives beside it. Migration 0014, PUT/DELETE .../evaluations/{id}/override on program:write, Override chip + control on the record, Overridden label on the results list. No change to reviewer-scope.ts, no Marquee-hosted inference (R3), no "AI" in user-facing strings (R5).

BROWSER VALIDATION (c11 browser against npx vite dev, organizer session, seeded "Taming 40-Minute CI"):
1. Agent 4.50 [Agent] and human 4.20 render side by side with rationales.
2. Clicked Override score on the agent row, entered 3.1 + reason, saved.
3. RELOADED — override persisted: [Override] chip, 3.10 governing, "Overridden by AIE Program Committee · Triage agent scored 4.50 · <reason>", agent rationale intact.
4. Results list agrees: "Overridden · Triage agent · Agent · 3.10", human aggregate still 4.21.
5. Clear override + reload restores 4.50 with no chip.
6. No reflow: measured in the live DOM, chip slot 70px and control row 26px in BOTH states. The first measurement caught a 6px jump and the slot was widened until they matched.

Screenshots: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-atin-Projects-Stage11-deployments-Marquee-worktrees-mrq-149-agent-eval-score/a361de9e-cfce-4e96-bf53-9e5374b34092/scratchpad/before-override.png and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-atin-Projects-Stage11-deployments-Marquee-worktrees-mrq-149-agent-eval-score/a361de9e-cfce-4e96-bf53-9e5374b34092/scratchpad/after-override.png

GATE (local; CI on main is red on a 5-minute npm test timeout, not an assertion): tsc --noEmit, vite build, schema-verify (105 FKs), check:design, check:api, check:routes, check:seed, trace:ac all pass. npm test 187/187 pass. pr-gate: every check passed. Both suites landed over their time budget on a contended box (load 12-39 on 16 cores) — time only, and the wrapper says so itself.

DEVIATION TO FLAG: MRQ-149 had no pre-minted ACs, so the five new tests carry the CONTRACT prefix (trace:ac requires AC-n or CONTRACT). Delegators do not mint ACs.

data.body:
## Code review landed: PASS (4 MINOR, 3 NIT). Artifact `art_01KZW4GX5PR6MJ6BNW1KBDT0S4`.

**Trap for anyone reading this ticket:** `lattice review-status MRQ-149` still prints
"Review FAILED ... timed out after 600s". That is the **stale record from the first
attempt at 22:20:35**, read out of `failures.jsonl`. The third run completed and stored an
artifact. My own background monitor was fooled by it and I nearly relayed a false timeout.
Read the artifact, not `review-status`.

#137 merged as `1f61a95d`. Post-merge verification on real main: all 13 files landed; the
capabilities block on `github/main` still carries `&& canWriteProgram` on `can_schedule`
(779), `can_publish` (784) and `can_unpublish` (785) — MRQ-155's authorization tightening
survived the merge, not just my rebase; one `0014`, one `0015`; and my suites run
**20/20 against merged main**, which also carries `6854107e` that I never had on my branch.

## Findings, and where each is being fixed

| # | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|
| MINOR 4 | An off-scale override replaced the whole record with "Record unavailable" — dead-end-shaped, in the flow ABS-14 exists to make walkable | **PR-A #156** |
| MINOR 1 | `override_score` on the wire but absent from the published schema, falsifying the submission pack's "no undocumented endpoint" claim one level down | **PR-A #156** |
| MINOR 2 | Plan summary's `highest_score`/`wide_spread` read raw `score`; two organizer screens disagree after an override | PR-B |
| MINOR 3 | A reviewer's revision leaves a stale override governing, silently — defensible rule, but an accident of which columns the upsert lists | PR-B (keep + pin + comment) |
| NIT 5 | `.agent-review-label` reserves no width, so "Agent score" → "Overridden" shifts the row | PR-B |
| NIT 6 | Docstring overstated the layout guarantee | fixed in PR-A |
| NIT 7 | The weighted-interaction aggregate test my plan promised was not written | PR-B |

## The red gate the reviewer hit was mine, not environmental

They saw 3 failures in `tests/unit/r2/uploads-routes.test.ts` and correctly traced them to a
`.dev.vars` carrying `LOCAL_UPLOAD_SHIM=1`. **That `.dev.vars` was mine** — I write it for
browser validation and delete it after, and their run overlapped the window. `DEPLOY.md`
warns "delete `.dev.vars` before running the gate"; what it does not say is that in a
multi-agent tree, someone *else's* `.dev.vars` can redden *your* gate. My own gate runs and
CI on `33913df1` were clean, so the merged code is unaffected — but I left a landmine in a
shared worktree and someone stepped on it.

## PR-A (#156) validation

Drove the reviewer's exact scenario rather than reasoning about it: opened the override
form (`min="1" max="5"`, label `Override score · 1–5`), **typed 9** → inline "This plan
scores 1–5.", Save disabled, record still standing with both evaluation rows. Then the
happy path: set 2, saved, reloaded, override persists at 2.00 with the agent's 4.50 and
rationale intact. `pr-gate` **`"status": "pass"`, 45,704ms against 120,000ms** at load 2.

Worth recording: my first schema test looked in `components.schemas` and failed against a
*working* fix — the agent review is inlined under `SubmissionListItem`, not a named
component. Rewrote it to assert the real location, then verified it fails without the
one-line fix before restoring. A regression test I have not watched fail is not one.

## Both follow-up PRs are filed. Every code-review finding is addressed.

- **PR-A — #156** (base `main`): MINOR 4 + MINOR 1, the two judge-facing ones. **Merge this first.**
- **PR-B — #157** (base `mrq-149-followup`, stacked): MINOR 2, MINOR 3, NIT 5, NIT 7, and `docs/evidence/mrq-149/`.

NIT 6 was fixed in PR-A — I rewrote that docstring while editing the component, so it now
claims only what is reserved (the chip and Clear slots) and admits the row grows by the
superseded line and the open form.

| Finding | Fix | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| MINOR 4 — off-scale override replaced the record with an error page | Plan scale travels with each evaluation; `min`/`max` on the input; override writes report inline and leave the record standing | Typed `9` in the live UI → "This plan scores 1–5.", Save disabled, **2 evaluation rows still present** |
| MINOR 1 — `override_score` on the wire, absent from the schema | One line on `submissionAgentReviewSchema` | Test asserts it at its real inlined location; **verified failing without the fix** |
| MINOR 2 — plan summary headlined a superseded score | `COALESCE` in `MAX`, the outer comparison, and the correlated `AVG` | Test: summary `4.2` → override → `2` |
| MINOR 3 — stale override survived a revision, accidentally | Stated in the upsert; the rule is now deliberate | Pinned both ways: override survives, reviewer's revision still recorded, clearing restores the *current* value |
| NIT 5 — results list shifted on override | `min-width: 74px` on `.agent-review-label` | Measured live: `Agent score` 74px, `Overridden` 74px |
| NIT 7 — weighted-interaction branch untested | Fixture with `criteria_scores`, then overridden | `{4, weighted: true}` → `{2, weighted: false}` |

Suite is **11/11**. `pr-gate` **`"status": "pass"`** on both branches inside budget — 45.7s
for PR-A, 42.5s for PR-B, on a box at load 2–4.

## Two things I got wrong and corrected, recorded because they are the useful part

**My first schema test could not have failed for the right reason.** It swept
`components.schemas` looking for any object carrying `override_score`; the agent review is
inlined under `SubmissionListItem.properties.agent_reviews.items`, not a named component,
so it failed against a *working* fix. I probed the served document, found the real location,
rewrote the assertion to point at it — then removed the one-line fix and watched the
corrected test fail (1 failed / 7 passed) before restoring. A regression test I have not
watched fail is not a regression test.

**The reviewer's red gate was my `.dev.vars`, not the environment.** I write it for browser
validation and delete it after; their run overlapped the window, and `LOCAL_UPLOAD_SHIM=1`
reddened three R2 tests that have nothing to do with this diff. `DEPLOY.md` warns to delete
it before running the gate — what it does not say is that in a multi-agent tree someone
else's `.dev.vars` can redden *your* gate. Worth adding there.

## Landed. #156 merged as `29300ecf` and is the build under sbek round 4.

Eval Round Prep deployed `29300ecf` at 23:48Z and fired round 4 against it, so the
off-scale fix is in the evaluated build. No redeploy pending. **#157** (`400bab9c`) is open,
green-gated, rebased onto main, and affects no eval-scored behaviour.

## Correction worth carrying forward: verify the schema at `/api/openapi.json`, never `/api/docs`

My PR-A body claimed R53 is scored by a judge reading `/api/docs`. That is imprecise in a way
that manufactures a false alarm, and Eval Round Prep nearly lost time to it.

`/api/docs` is a server-rendered reference **table of operations** — method, path, summary —
that links the machine-readable document through `<link rel="alternate">`
(`src/api/openapi.ts:180`). It embeds no schema properties, so `curl /api/docs | grep
override_score` returns **0 whether or not the field is documented**. The field lives at:

```
/api/openapi.json → components.schemas.SubmissionListItem
                    .properties.agent_reviews.items.properties.override_score
```

Fixed in three places so nobody re-derives it: the #156 PR body now carries the correct path
and says why the grep misleads; the schema test in #157 names the trap where someone checking
"is this documented?" will actually be standing; and it is recorded here.

This is the second time on this ticket that a check aimed at the wrong surface produced a
confident wrong answer — the first was my own schema test sweeping `components.schemas` for
an inlined object. Same shape of error both times: the assertion ran, passed or failed
cleanly, and was measuring nothing.

## Every code-review finding is now closed

| Finding | State |
|---|---|
| MINOR 4 — off-scale override destroyed the record | **merged, deployed, in the evaluated build** |
| MINOR 1 — `override_score` undocumented | **merged, deployed** |
| MINOR 2 — plan summary headlined a superseded score | #157 |
| MINOR 3 — stale override across a revision, accidental | #157, now deliberate and pinned |
| NIT 5 — results list shifted on override | #157, 74px both states |
| NIT 6 — docstring overstated the layout guarantee | merged in #156 |
| NIT 7 — weighted-interaction branch untested | #157 |
| evidence artifacts | #157, `docs/evidence/mrq-149/` |

## MRQ-149 closed. ABS-14's feature is merged, deployed, and in the build under evaluation.

| Artifact | State |
|---|---|
| **#137** — the chair's override | merged `1f61a95d` |
| **#156** — off-scale override no longer destroys the record; `override_score` documented | merged `29300ecf`, **deployed 23:48Z, the build sbek round 4 is browsing** |
| **#157** — remaining review findings + `docs/evidence/mrq-149/` | open at `43fdd985`, green-gated, held for the human merge gate; affects no eval-scored behaviour |

Every finding from the independent review (`art_01KZW4GX5PR6MJ6BNW1KBDT0S4`, verdict PASS) is
closed: MINOR 1, 4 and NIT 6 merged; MINOR 2, 3 and NIT 5, 7 in #157.

## What this ticket actually taught, beyond the feature

**Three checks on this ticket ran cleanly while measuring nothing.** They are worth recording
together because they were indistinguishable from working checks at a glance:

1. A schema test sweeping `components.schemas` for an object that is *inlined* under
   `SubmissionListItem` — failed against a working fix.
2. `curl /api/docs | grep override_score` — returns 0 whether or not the field is
   documented, because `/api/docs` renders an operations table and links the spec via
   `<link rel="alternate">`. It cannot pass. Verify at `/api/openapi.json`.
3. The MINOR 3 test reaching the row with raw SQL — never executing the upsert whose
   `DO UPDATE SET` column list was the entire behaviour under test.

All three failed the same question: **name the input that turns this red.** That
interrogative — Eval Round Prep's sharpening of "a check that cannot fail is not a check" —
is a better gate than the assertion, because it cannot be answered with a nod.

The settled proof is sabotage-and-restore, in order: add the mutation the test claims to
catch, watch it go red, restore, confirm green, **confirm `git diff` is empty**. That last
step is the one that gets skipped.

## Two hazards for the next agent in this tree

- **`.dev.vars` is a landmine in a shared worktree.** I write it for browser validation and
  delete it after; a reviewer's gate run overlapped that window and `LOCAL_UPLOAD_SHIM=1`
  reddened three R2 tests unrelated to the diff. `DEPLOY.md` says to delete it before
  gating; what it does not say is that someone *else's* can redden *your* gate.
- **`lattice review-status MRQ-149` prints a stale 600s timeout** from the first of three
  review attempts, read out of `failures.jsonl`, while a completed artifact exists. My own
  monitor was fooled and I nearly relayed a false failure. Read the artifact.
